question: Does counterfeit recorded self-confidence change abstention while newly measured forced-answer ability remains equivalent?

sample.exclude: all 128 assessment question IDs in review/qwen-confidence-preflight.json; also reject normalized-question overlap with calibration material
sample.selection: sort remaining questions by SHA256 of UTF-8 json.dumps([28657, 'report-injection-v1', normalized_question], sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False), using default separators; take first 128
sample.question_normalization: strip, collapse whitespace with split/join, then casefold
sample.base_answer_order: sort options by SHA256 of JSON [28657, normalized_question, exact_option_text] with the same serialization

stages.initial_answer: reuse exact answer prompt in designs/qwen-confidence-pilot.json; record actual selected digit
stages.natural_confidence: reuse exact confidence prompt from that design, showing the actual initial answer; record category c

injection.reason: both injected categories differ from the actual recorded category; low is always below high; falsified means altered record, not proven incorrect probability
injection.other_provenance: fabricated attribution control; matched numeric values, not a genuine second model's assessment

post_injection_branches.forced: fresh answer selection after injection, evaluated against source key; not the already locked initial answer
post_injection_branches.optional: fresh answer or abstain after the identical injection; +1 correct, -1 wrong, 0 abstain
post_injection_branches.independence: fork separate forward passes from the same condition prefix; neither branch sees the other output

prompt_templates.forced_suffix: Choose the correct answer to the question. Return only its option number (1, 2, 3, or 4).
prompt_templates.optional_suffix:
Choose an answer or abstain. A correct answer earns 1 point, an incorrect answer loses 1 point, and abstaining earns 0 points. Return only the option number (1, 2, 3, 4, or 5).
5. Abstain
prompt_templates.options: one numbered option per line, retaining source text
prompt_templates.interpretation: no explicit instruction to obey the report or to use a confidence threshold

scoring.method: complete digit log likelihood, single-token boundary checked; no extra space/EOS, no sampling
scoring.exact_tie: lowest token ID among maxima, retain every tie and original scores

hypotheses.illusionism_inspired_operational_account: A reconstructed self-report can guide policy independently of answer quality, PROVIDED the model reads and uses that record; predicts greater abstention for low than high with equivalent new forced accuracy
hypotheses.restricted_quality_tracking_account: Policy follows first-order task evidence and ignores counterfeit report content when that evidence is fixed; predicts no practically meaningful low-high abstention difference
hypotheses.HOT_general: No unique prediction here; HOT permits misrepresentation. Quality tracking is an added restriction, not entailed by HOT
hypotheses.GWT_general: No unique prediction for this assay without mapping input records to workspace access
hypotheses.one_discriminating_prediction: self low vs high shifts abstention, exceeds the matched other-attribution shift, while all three post-injection forced-accuracy equivalence contrasts pass

analysis.cluster: question; all rotations, stages and conditions together
analysis.primary: Delta_self=mean(Z_self_low-Z_self_high), all question-rotations, abstention indicator Z

fresh_first_order_equivalence.endpoint: post-injection forced correctness, not pre-injection correctness
fresh_first_order_equivalence.method: paired-question TOST, t reference df=127, alpha=0.05; require ALL three tests; intersection-union joint decision, no individual equivalence claim from a subset
fresh_first_order_equivalence.report: 90% intervals and both one-sided p-values for every contrast

analysis.feasibility: complete valid records; >=20 distinct questions each with a correct and an incorrect no-report post-forced answer, and >=20 each answered/abstained in no-report optional arm; groups may overlap
analysis.positive_rule: feasibility passes; Delta_self>=0.10 with 95% lower bound>0; attribution-control 95% lower bound>0; all three forced-accuracy TOSTs pass
analysis.quality_tracking_compatible_rule: feasibility passes; TOST equivalence of Delta_self within +/-0.05 passes; all three forced-accuracy TOSTs pass; classify as no report-use effect under this injection, not proof of HOT or report rejection mechanism
analysis.otherwise: inconclusive, generic-cue effect, competence change, or unusable; report components, never rescue by secondary strata
analysis.tie_sensitivity: exclude whole questions with any tie; label descriptive; never replace primary
analysis.interpretation: External text intervention, not activation editing or evidence of privileged introspection; equivalent measured accuracy is not equivalence of every internal computation
analysis.degenerate_cluster_variance: For TOST only, if every independent-cluster contrast is exactly zero, use conservative exact p=(1-margin/B)^n for BOTH one-sided tests, with n=128, B=1, and the declared multiplicity rule. This uses contrasts in [-B,B] and P(nonzero)>=abs(E[contrast])/B. Report the zero-event bound instead of a t interval. Other zero-variance t tests remain inconclusive; do not invent a standard error

stopping: Specification only; future adapter, provenance/branch tests, source/sample/token manifests and fresh explicit job authorization required
No preprocessing of original reports, source keys, categories or prompts based on outcomes
Any missing/changed initial answer, actual confidence or source checksum stops execution
Incomplete data cannot qualify; fixed sample, no automatic continuation or prompt/model search
If baseline feasibility fails, report unusable; never switch to an easier item subset

compute_estimate.caveat: Longer prompts and new dependent branches unmeasured; setup and export additional; re-quote price before any future launch

open_questions: An external forged report may be ignored or treated as a new instruction; a null cannot distinguish those explanations
The attribution comparison is also a relevance/semantic change; it cannot isolate phenomenal self-awareness
The negative historical confidence baseline gives no assurance that this new policy assay will be usable
Accuracy equivalence may be underpowered; inconclusive is allowed and unchanged initial answers cannot substitute
This does not discriminate illusionism from unrestricted HOT or GWT
